claims.text: Pure single-phase ZrB2 conventionally requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Conventional sintering of pure ZrB2 above 2300 °C results in incomplete densification.
Conventionally prepared pure ZrB2 retains porosity and structural weaknesses under service conditions.
A trace reactive boron-rich sintering aid can form a transient liquid phase in ZrB2 during sintering at 2100–2200 °C.
The transient liquid phase enhances particle rearrangement.
The transient liquid phase enhances mass transport during sintering.
Adding the sintering aid permits ZrB2 densification at 2100–2200 °C.
Adding the sintering aid suppresses pore formation and produces a more uniform microstructure.
Sintering-aid-treated ZrB2 prepared at 2100–2200 °C will have greater densification than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Sintering-aid-treated ZrB2 will contain fewer or no pores after sintering than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
The improved microstructural uniformity will increase the mechanical strength of ZrB2.
The improved microstructural uniformity will increase resistance to liquid-bath-induced degradation.
Sintering-aid-treated ZrB2 will have better structural stability during long-duration liquid plating bath exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Microstructural pores formed during elevated-temperature liquid plating bath exposure lead to mechanical degradation.
The additive may form secondary phases or leave residual contaminants.
The proposed comparison uses conventionally sintered ZrB2 above 2300 °C as the control and additive-containing ZrB2 sintered at 2100–2200 °C as the intervention group.
